verdict: Afterglow is held with real discipline: ember appears only as light and the wavy fluff underline (zero stray hues in a computed-style audit), Inter only, one wordmark from nav to edge-lit footer, and the lowercase heycape voice gives the page an X-native personality of its own. What keeps it a hair under 9.5 is a handful of small finish issues a brand lead would catch on the first scroll: bright headings ghosting through the sticky nav, a cramped phone notification at 390, and a type scale with too many near-duplicate sizes.
to_95: Make the sticky nav opaque enough that 30-72px white headings and struck draft text do not read through it while scrolling (raise the #08090A fill to about 0.88-0.92 alpha and/or increase the blur), so the wordmark always sits on clean ground.

At 390/360, give the lock-screen notification in the 8:40 AM phone clear air: it wraps to three lines and its bottom edge touches the heycape avatar/name row beneath. Shorten to two lines on phones or push the feed down 10-12px.
Consolidate the type scale: 13/13.5/14/15, 16/17/18 and 22/24/25/26 are all live. Collapse to one size per step (e.g. 13, 15, 17, 22) so small text reads as one system.

issues.where: Sticky nav at 1440 and 390 while scrolling (e.g. over 'Lowercase and all.', the 'so basically' draft, the phone notification)
issues.problem: The nav glass is translucent enough that large white headings and card text stay legible as ghosts behind the wordmark and nav links. It muddies the one place the wordmark lives and is visible in the first scroll.
issues.fix: Raise nav background to rgba(8,9,10,0.88-0.92) once scrolled and/or increase backdrop blur to ~24px with saturate; keep the hairline. Verify no heading is legible behind it at any scroll position.

issues.where: 'Say it at 11 PM / Post it at 8:40 AM' phone at 390 and 360, settled state and reduced motion
issues.problem: The notification wraps to three lines on phones, so its bottom edge sits flush against (about 3px into) the heycape avatar and name row. At 1440 it sits cleanly; on the phone it looks cramped.
issues.fix: On <=480px either shorten the notification to two lines ('Your 8:40 post is getting replies. Answers drafted.') or add 10-12px top offset to the feed post beneath it.

issues.problem: 20 distinct font sizes are in use, with near-duplicates: 13/13.5/14/15, 16/17/18, 22/24/25/26. Heading tiers (30/40/72/99) are clean; the small-text tier is not, and it shows as slight inconsistency between captions, meta rows and body across bento cards.
issues.fix: Map to a fixed scale (12, 13, 15, 17, 22, 30, 40, 72, 99). Fold 13.5 and 14 into 13 or 15, 16 and 18 into 17, 24/25/26 into 22 or a single 25.

issues.problem: The four-colour Google G is the only non-ember hue on the entire page; inside an otherwise monochrome glass sheet it pulls the eye away from the white primary 'Continue with X' pill.
issues.fix: Keep the official G (required for the mark) but reduce it to 16px and drop its button to the quieter frosted style already used; or, if the founder prefers, lead with X and email only and place Google as a text-weight third option.

issues.problem: At 1440 the edge-lit giant wordmark is a strong sign-off. On phones it is so dim and so heavily cropped (about the top 60% of the letters, ember rim almost invisible) that it reads as a rendering artefact rather than a brand moment, and the small wordmark plus tagline that sit above it on desktop are absent.
issues.fix: On <=480px raise the fill/rim opacity one step (rim to roughly 0.5 ember) and show at least to the baseline of the x-height letters, or restore the small wordmark and one-line tagline above the links.
